newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy BCI shares rise after Napoli denial.
newsitem.headline: Italy BCI shares rise after Napoli denial.

text.p: Shares in Italy's Banca Commerciale Italiana (BCI) rose after the group's managing director Luigi Fausti denied that the Milan-based bank was planning any action over the Banco di Napoli.
Shares in BCI closed up 2.5 percent at 2,875 lire after a high of 2,930 lire with over 7.2 million shares traded.

Market speculation has suggested that BCI might bid for the struggling Naples-based bank, which is due for privatisation by the end of the year, but BCI has in the past always declined to comment on the talk.

The Italian government hopes to privatise the heavily-indebted bank by the end of the year. Potential buyers of the bank have until November 18 to declare an interest in the sale of an initial 60 percent of the Naples bank.
Dealers said there was relief that BCI was not to become involved in what could be an expensive venture to take over and then return to profit the loss-making southern bank.
BCI's Fausti told reporters, "BCI has not planned and does not plan any intervention regarding Banco di Napoli."
